units.title: Safe, Hygienic and Secure Baking Environment

learning_outcomes.description: 1.0 Implement food safety and hygiene regulations in a baking environment

performance_criteria.description: Interpret food safety guidelines
Interpret organizational hygiene policies in relation to regulatory standards
Demonstrate personal hygiene protocols, including wound management
Apply appropriate protective equipment (PPE) selection
Identify potential physical, chemical, and biological hazards
Adopt organisational strategies for prevention of the hazards

learning_outcomes.description: 2.0 Monitor sanitation of the baking area and equipment

performance_criteria.description: Formulate cleaning schedules for different areas, surfaces and baking equipment
Utilize appropriate cleaning agents and disinfectants.
Monitor the cleaning and sanitation procedures.
Manage safe disposal of bakery waste
Implement preventive pest-control measures

learning_outcomes.description: 3.0 Manage workplace security and hazard control

performance_criteria.description: Im plement standard operating procedures (SOPs) for operating equipment (e.g., large mixers, industrial ovens)
Se cure proper storage for bakery equipment, raw and packaging materials and finished products
Implement organisation’s emergency action plans, including fire safety, accident reporting, and first-aid protocols
Adopt Government regulations on health and safety in Industry (OHS Act 2012)

learning_outcomes.description: 1.0 Coordinate Team Activities in the Bakery

performance_criteria.description: Allocate tasks to team members based on skill level and production requirements
Develop daily production schedules for team members
Monitor workflow to ensure timely completion of tasks.
Adjust task allocation to address changes in production demand or staff availability
Ensure compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) during team operations.

learning_outcomes.description: 2.0 Communicate Effectively within the Team

performance_criteria.description: Use clear and professional communication when giving instructions.
Facilitate team briefings and debriefings before and after production.
Provide constructive feedback to team members to improve performance.
Actively listen and respond appropriately to team members’ concerns
Maintain proper documentation and communication records where necessary.

learning_outcomes.description: 3.0 Demonstrate leadership and supervision skills

performance_criteria.description: Lead by example in maintaining hygiene, safety, and quality standards.
Motivate team members to achieve production targets.
Supervise team members to ensure adherence to processes and procedures
Identify training needs and support skill development within the team.
Evaluate team performance and recommend improvements

learning_outcomes.description: 4.0 Resolve conflict and promote team cohesion

performance_criteria.description: Identify sources of conflict within the team promptly.
Apply appropriate conflict resolution techniques to address issues.
Encourage mutual respect and positive working relationships among team members.
Resolve disputes fairly and professionally.
Foster an inclusive and supportive team environment.
Escalate unresolved issues to management promptly

units.title: Communication System in a Work in Environment

learning_outcomes.description: 1.0 Use a Non-complex Communication System in a Work environment.

performance_criteria.description: Use simple verbal means to pass on necessary information
Use non-verbal means to pass on necessary information
Interpret symbols and signs appropriately

learning_outcomes.description: 2.0 Identify the source of information in a Work Environment

performance_criteria.description: Locate the Source of information in an organization or Work Environment
Relate appropriately with the source of information
Use the various information flow systems in a work environment
Use information to avoid challenges in a work situation
Report findings in accordance to procedures in a work environment

learning_outcomes.description: 3.0 Demonstrate the means of communication in a work environment

performance_criteria.description: Locate the various communication equipment in the work environment
Use the various communication equipment effectively in a work environment
Pass information effectively to the right personnel
Pass information effectively using symbols, signs and codes
Follow instructions in line with ethics of the work environment.

learning_outcomes.description: 1.0 Understand capacity planning concepts and techniques in baking

performance_criteria.description: Identify the capacity of equipment (e.g., oven, mixer, generator, packaging lines)
Explain capacity planning strategies (e.g., increasing batch sizes, overtime, outsourcing
Apply capacity planning strategies that eliminate wastage

learning_outcomes.description: 2.0 Determine capacity requirements for bakery products

performance_criteria.description: Analyze demand forecast for bread, cakes and pastries.
Identify capacity constraints (e.g., oven availability, skilled labor)
Identify measures to overcome constraints in 2.2

learning_outcomes.description: 3.0 Develop capacity plan

performance_criteria.description: Formulate a production schedule that aligns dough/batter preparation and baking times with fluctuating order volumes
Evaluate the operational impact of alternative plans such as night shifts versus early morning scaling
Allocate staff efficiently throughout the production shift

learning_outcomes.description: 4.0 Monitor and review capacity performance

performance_criteria.description: Adopt Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) such as yield of usable product per batch and energy consumption per loaf
Implement logging mechanisms to track actual production output against the planned schedule
Recommend corrective actions or adjustments, such as mixing sequences when ingredients variations occur

learning_outcomes.description: 1.0 Understand the functional properties of basic ingredients

performance_criteria.description: Identify the chemical composition, such as protein, moisture and starch in different flour
Explain specific applications of 1.1 in dough and batter production
Explain how nutritive and non-nutritive sweeteners influence moisture retention, structure and crust color in baked goods
Differentiate the functions of the various fats and emulsifiers (e.g. butter, shortening, oil) regarding fat crystallization, aeration and shortening power

learning_outcomes.description: 2.0 Evaluate role of leavening agents/ liquid in baking formulation.

performance_criteria.description: Apply the appropriate use and activation requirements of leavening agents for different products
State the effect of liquid temperature, pH and hydration levels on enzyme activity and gluten development
Calculate baker’s percentages to adjust recipes for scaling and formulation balance.

learning_outcomes.description: 3.0 Apply knowledge of basic and optional ingredients to modify baked products.

performance_criteria.description: State the function of binders, thickeners and preservatives in maintaining product quality and shelf life.
Formulate Various bread varieties using optional ingredients such as butter bread, chocolate bread, sardine bread.
Formulate bread varieties for dietary restrictions – such as low sugar, wheat bread, baguette.
Formulate Various pastry varieties using optional ingredients.

learning_outcomes.description: 1.0 Maintain bakery equipment and work environment

performance_criteria.description: Implement good manufacturing practices (GMPs)
Carry out pre and post productions checks on weighing, measuring, and temperature-monitoring devices
Explain Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) protocols for the cleaning and sanitizing of the workspace

learning_outcomes.description: 2.0 Select, weigh, and mix a variety of bakery ingredients to precise specifications

performance_criteria.description: Adjust ingredient quantities to accommodate different batch sizes and scaling factors.
Evaluate the quality and freshness of raw materials and ingredients, reporting any non-conformities before use.
Use mixing techniques to create diverse doughs, laminated doughs, and batters.

learning_outcomes.description: 3.0 Manage fermentation, Proofing, and baking environments.

performance_criteria.description: Regulate humidity and temperature in the proofing cabinet to control fermentation rates precisely.
Adjust baking parameters (temperature profiles, steam injection, and airflow) for various product types
Identify common defects during the baking process.
Troubleshoot common defects during the baking process, implementing corrective actions in real time.

learning_outcomes.description: 4.0 Implement Quality Control and Post-Baking Procedures

performance_criteria.description: Evaluate finished products against sensory, texture, and visual quality standards.
Manage the cooling, slicing, and finishing (glazing, icing, or dusting) processes to maintain structural integrity
manage post-baking processes including cooling, wrapping, and storage

units.title: Handling, Packaging and Labelling Baked Products

learning_outcomes.description: 1.0 Prepare packaging and labelling materials

performance_criteria.description: Select appropriate packaging materials based on the size and type of the product.
Inspect all packaging materials for cleanliness, integrity, and damage prior to use.
Prepare labelling machinery or formulate clear, legible, and accurate labels containing mandatory product information
Calculate the necessary quantity of packaging materials required to meet production targets without excessive waste

learning_outcomes.description: 2.0 Package baked products safely and hygienically

performance_criteria.description: Check that baked products have cooled to the appropriate temperature before packaging
Handle products using sanitary techniques (e.g., using tongs, gloves, or clean workspace surfaces)
Seal packaged product securely using suitable techniques (e.g., heat-sealing, twisting, or vacuum-sealing) ]
Pack items uniformly into primary and secondary containers, verifying product count and quality standards

learning_outcomes.description: 3.0 Label packages with accurate product and regulatory information

performance_criteria.description: Use packaging Label that conform with regulatory standard
Fix labels accurately and securely to the packaging in accordance with organizational guidelines
Maintain uniformity of labelling across all packaged products.

units.title: Display and Sale of Bakery Products

learning_outcomes.description: 1.0 Display Bakery Products

performance_criteria.description: Inspect bakery products for quality, freshness, and structural integrity prior to display.
Transfer finished products using appropriate tools and techniques to prevent damage or contamination
Display products to optimize visual appeal and product accessibility while maintaining appropriate temperature controls (where applicable).
Attach accurate and compliant pricing to all products or display units.

learning_outcomes.description: 2.0 Advise Customers and Process Sales

performance_criteria.description: Greet customers in a courteous and professional manner
Provide accurate information to customers regarding product ingredients, flavour profiles, and dietary suitability (e.g., gluten-free, vegan, or nut-free options).
Process sales transactions correctly using standard point-of-sale (POS) equipment, Cash or digital systems

learning_outcomes.description: 3.0 Maintain Hygienic, Safety, and Stock Control

performance_criteria.description: Monitor stock levels and apply the First-In, First-Out (FIFO) method to ensure the freshness and rotation of baked goods.
Monitor stock levels and apply the First-Expire-First-Out (FEFO) method to ensure the freshness and rotation of baked goods.
Maintain the cleanliness and sanitation of the display counters, shelving, and surrounding retail environment throughout the shift
Dispose of unsellable or expired bakery items safely in accordance with waste management and environmental policies
Address customer feedback or complaints promptly and professionally.

learning_outcomes.description: 1.0 Understand the principles of inventory management in a commercial bakery

performance_criteria.description: Explain the importance of stock rotation (e.g., FEFO, FIFO) for perishable and temperature-sensitive bakery ingredients
Describe different types of inventory (raw materials, semi-finished, finished products
Analyse inventory control systems (FIFO, LIFO, FEFO)
Identify key documentation used in inventory management (stock cards, bin cards, requisition forms)

learning_outcomes.description: 2.0 Implement procedures for receiving and storing bakery stocks

performance_criteria.description: Inspect incoming deliveries against purchase orders, verifying quantity, quality, temperature, and expiration dates
Store ingredients and packaging materials according to organizational food safety standards and manufacturer guidelines
Maintain complete and accurate records of received, transferred, and discarded stock

learning_outcomes.description: 3.0 Monitor and control daily inventory levels and usage.

performance_criteria.description: Conduct physical stock counts and reconcile discrepancies between actual stock and recorded balances
Calculate ingredient usage and yield against production schedules to identify variances and prevent shortages
Report damaged, expired, or spoiled stock following workplace and environmental regulations

learning_outcomes.description: 4.0 Monitor inventory usage and control cost

performance_criteria.description: Track stock movement and usage rates in production
Calculate stock levels and reorder levels
Use inventory data to identify trends and variances
Implement cost control measures to reduce waste and losses

learning_outcomes.description: 1.0 Prepare accurate bakery production records

performance_criteria.description: Record production data accurately (quantities, time, process stages)
Document ingredient usage and stock levels correctly
Maintain batch records for different bakery products
Ensure records are clear, legible, and completed in real-time
Use appropriate formats (manual or digital systems) for documentation

learning_outcomes.description: 2.0 Apply documentation to support food safety and quality assurance

performance_criteria.description: Record critical control points (CCPs) in line with Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) principles
Document temperature controls for storage, baking, and cooling processes
Maintain cleaning and sanitation logs according to hygiene standards
Report deviations and corrective actions accurately
Ensure documentation supports compliance with food safety regulations

learning_outcomes.description: 3.0 Organize bakery documentation systems

performance_criteria.description: Organize records for easy retrieval and audit purposes
Store documentation securely (physical and digital formats)
Update records regularly to reflect current operations
Ensure confidentiality and integrity of bakery record
Implement basic filing and archiving systems
